shore-day.note: the fire is painted OUT (dead coals, goats loose); the band is the SUN's path -- the anchors hold, the night tint does not, so the day state halves them rather than recolours

emissives.note: the campfire on the beach; centre + radius + tint are shore-bloom.png's own measured profile. OUT in shore-day (the state paints dead coals): gain 0.
the moonpath where it enters the inlet (top third of the glint band)
the brightest reach of the path, mid-band between the ships and the far bank
the path dying against the beach shallows (bottom third)

bloom.note: the measured additive fire bloom; pulse its opacity with the fire emissive, gain 0 in shore-day

fog.note: the waterline breath; alpha feather baked in, no CSS mask needed

fireBloom.model: falloff = median (R-B) profile over the sand sector, base = its own tail (r 170..190), tail clamped to 0, boxcar(5)x2 + monotone envelope against facet ringing; tint = (sand at r 20..45 - sand at r 115..145) / their warm-excess delta, so the sand albedo cancels and what remains is the light
fireBloom.note: additive bloom; ships as a screen layer the set pulses

moonpath.model: lum>150 & B>R-12 in the inlet window, split at the 33rd/66th y-percentiles; luminance-weighted centroid + 1.8x rms radius
moonpath.note: a specular band is not a halo: it breathes as EMIS anchors, the way street chained bay -> spill -> wet

fog.tintModel: 0.5*glintMean + 0.5*(backdrop hue raised to 0.8x glint luminance); backdrop = median of plate px with lum<45
fog.band: gaussian in y about 506, sigma 54; x ramps [380.0, 470.0] up, [1080.0, 1180.0] down
fog.note: screen-blended, drifts; feather baked into the alpha so no CSS mask is needed (street shipped the seam, sec street.js)
